transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things with my house have gotten really bad, and people keep telling me it’s just paperwork or missed payments, but that doesn’t feel right to me. I know how it sounds, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but for almost two years I’ve been seeing signs that the bank, the loan servicer, and even some people at my job have been kind of working together to push me out of my house. They can show me papers, but that doesn’t really change what I’ve noticed.
Besides these suspicions about your house and job, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that others didn't seem to notice?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get tired and stressed, and sometimes I’m more alert to noises around the house than I probably used to be, but I wouldn’t say I’m hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there. That’s not really what this is. Does that make sense?

Over these past two years, have you had any stretches of time—separate from these concerns about your house—where you felt unusually elated, full of energy and barely needing sleep, or conversely, deeply depressed with low energy and loss of interest in things?

Um… I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I’ve had stress, obviously, and I’ve had days where I’m worn down or not sleeping great because I’m thinking about everything, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had some separate period where I was, like, unusually high or out of control or anything.

And depressed… I don’t know. I’ve been upset, sure, but I’m still going to work and trying to handle things. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you mean?

Aside from these concerns about your house and job, how are things going in other parts of your life—like your relationships with family or friends, taking care of yourself day-to-day, or your overall performance at work?

I mean… overall I think I’m functioning okay. I get up and go to work, I supervise my team, I do the schedules, deal with customer issues, that kind of thing. I’m taking care of myself day to day.

It’s more when something connects back to the house—like mail from the bank, phone calls, or certain paperwork at work—that things get harder for me. That’s when I start feeling like it’s all tied together again. But outside of that, I’m not just falling apart or anything. At least, I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Can you tell me more specifically when you first started noticing these connections between the bank, your job, and losing your house—was there a particular event or moment that made you first suspect this?

I think it really started when the foreclosure notices and the bank calls started… sort of taking over the house. That was, I guess, about a year and nine months ago now.

At first I tried to tell myself it was just paperwork and stress, but then it felt like it kept showing up in different places, even at work, and I started noticing those connections more. I don’t know if that’s too vague, but that’s about when it began.
Do you use alcohol, recreational drugs, or take any medications, and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions like thyroid problems or neurological issues?

Um… no, not really. I don’t use recreational drugs. I might have a drink once in a while, but nothing that feels like a problem.

Medications… I’m not on anything regular that I can think of. And I haven’t been told I have thyroid problems or anything neurological. At least not that I know of. Is that okay—like, is that what you mean?
